Present #2 • The Book

The Year I Got to Know You

Not a timeline. Just the person I’ve come to know, seen through my eyes.

PART 1 • THE BEGINNINGCHAPTER 1 • 1 OF 3
Part 1

The Beginning

Chapter 1

The beginning

Aarna

My life was in true turmoil when I met her. The worst part of it all, or so I thought. Almost like a kid who had wandered too far away from home, looking for something he couldn't quite put a name to. A home that, perhaps, never really existed in the first place. Maybe it wasn't even some sort of excitement or thrill he was chasing anymore. Maybe it was just a sense of belonging. A place where he could finally stop looking behind his shoulder and simply exist.

And she came in at that point. And just... stayed.

Stayed with me when I didn't even know who I was. Sat with me through all the things I couldn't make sense of, listened to stories I had probably told a hundred times, and somehow never made me feel like I was too much. She helped heal a child she never broke. And I don't think I'll ever quite be able to put into words what that means to me.

The home I had spent so long looking for came to me in her form. Not some perfect, untouched fairytale, but in the form of an exhausted teenager who, despite everything life has thrown at her, has somehow managed to hold on to that beautiful, carefree and rather playful side of herself. The part of her that laughs, gets excited over the smallest things, wants to be understood, wants to be cherished, and perhaps, more than anything, just wants to know that she matters. Someone who has learnt to keep so much to herself, not because she doesn't have things to say, but because she never wants her needs to become someone else's burden.

And oh, how I wish she knew just how much she deserves all those things. How she never has to earn the right to be cared for, how she doesn't have to be okay all the time, and how there's nothing troublesome about wanting to be loved.

And that's where I find myself now. Loving her, trying to help her see even a fraction of what I see in her, and reminding her that she deserves just as much tenderness as she gives to everyone else.

It's funny, really. I spent so long looking for a home, only to find myself wanting to build one with the very person who made me feel at home.

And somehow, while she was busy being my entire little universe, she became the reason I wanted to make hers a little brighter too.

✦
Chapter 2

Before We Became Us

Back in the days, when we used to be so close yet so far, sitting just a few steps away from each other, seeing each other almost every day, yet having no idea that we'd eventually become such a big part of each other's worlds. I saw her. Or rather, used to steal glances at her. Those little gazes from afar, admiring her beauty without ever really having the courage to let her know.

We did talk, of course. But it was mostly all that teasing, cringey stuff. The kind of conversations you'd look back at and go, "yeah I judged you". And now, when I look back and try to remember those little moments, I realise that perhaps it was just a mask I wore. A way to be around her, to feel her presence, to have some excuse to talk to her, while keeping my shyness and all those unspoken feelings safely tucked away. Because, as I used to believe, some feelings are better left unsaid.

And honestly? Sometimes, I think I'm glad I never said anything back then. Not because those feelings weren't worth expressing, but because perhaps they weren't meant to be expressed just yet. Everything has its own time, doesn't it? And now, when we're finally ready to be each other's safe space, I can't help but feel that this was the time we were supposed to find each other.

Once everything till 10th was over, I left. The entire state, in fact. Moved nearly 700 kilometres away, without even bothering with a proper goodbye. Not just to her, but to most of my friends. I simply... disappeared. Somewhere in the pursuit of building things up, I never quite realised how much of myself I was leaving behind. Slowly disappearing from people's minds, from places I once belonged to, and perhaps, most of all, from my own.

But she never quite forgot me.

Through Snapchat memes, through random reels, through those little things that probably didn't mean much at the time, I was still remembered. And I don't think she ever realised how much that meant to me. In a time when I felt like I was becoming a distant memory everywhere, there was still this little corner where I hadn't been forgotten. A little reminder that somewhere, somehow, I still existed in someone's world.

And that someone was her.

✦
Chapter 3

Somewhere Along the Way

Amidst all that chaos, we still managed to stay in touch. Through memes, reels, and all those little exchanges that kept us somewhere in each other's lives, came something more. Our conversations started getting deeper. Finally, conversations where I could feel myself actually thinking about someone other than myself. Caring about what you were going through, about your situation, about that feeling of wanting to be chosen. And strangely enough, I found myself genuinely wanting to understand it all.

It was strange because I rarely used to think about other people's feelings. Sometimes, not even my own. Actually, almost never my own, until you came along and slowly taught me how to. We discussed so many things, and somewhere in between all those conversations, I slipped in my confession. Those words that had remained unsaid for a couple of years finally found their way out. Or rather, through my keyboard.

And then came that one line. "It had a positive impact on me."

I don't think you realise how much those words meant to me. Something about them made me feel that something had shifted between us. That perhaps we weren't just two people exchanging memes and indulging in playful banter anymore. There was something more taking shape. Something that neither of us quite knew where to put a name to yet. It was us, slowly but surely, finding our way towards each other.

And somewhere along the way, I had already started choosing you. In the tiniest of ways, in places that might seem insignificant to anyone else, but meant something to me. Take those reels, for example. I used to get genuinely annoyed when people spammed me with them. But when it came to you? It was always different. There was this little thought that crossed my mind every single time. Ah, Aarna has sent me something. How would I not open it?

And then came 10th March. A day before my birthday. You sent me a picture. A picture of yourself.

And I don't know how to explain what that moment did to me. Perhaps it was the first time that the person I had spent so long admiring from afar was suddenly right there, letting me see a little more of her. And somehow, that one picture gave a face to a feeling I had been carrying for so long.

A feeling I would eventually learn to call home.

✦
Part 2

Getting to Know You

Chapter 4

The Way You Exist

I don't think my love realises just how many little things make her who she is. And I don't mean the obvious things, or the qualities that someone would notice after spending a few minutes with her. I'm talking about the really small things. The way she reacts to something, the way her face lights up when she's excited, the little things she gets happy about, the way she can be so quiet at one moment and then have so much to say the next. It's funny, really. If someone asked me to describe her, I'd probably have a hundred things to say, and somehow still feel like I've left out the most important ones.

One thing I've always loved about her is how playful she can be. She has this rather carefree side to her, this little version of herself that doesn't really worry about whether something looks cringe or whether it's silly. She just enjoys it. And I don't think she should ever have to worry about that. There's something genuinely nice about seeing someone enjoy the little things without having to make everything so serious. She likes cute things, little random things, and sometimes the most childish stuff can make her happy. And honestly, I find that side of her adorable. Not because it's something unusual, but because it's so naturally her.

She's also quite an interesting person to talk to. Around most people, she's more of a listener, but when she's comfortable, she can talk quite a lot. And I mean quite a lot. Sometimes she gets excited about something and just keeps going, and I could probably listen to her for ages. We switch between talking and listening so naturally that it's difficult to tell who's actually carrying the conversation. And then there are times when she knows exactly what she wants to say but can't quite get the words out. That's something I've noticed about her. Sometimes I try to put what I think she's trying to say into words, and she'll just respond with a yes or a no until we finally get it right. It's not that she doesn't know what she feels. Sometimes finding the right words just takes a little time.

And how can I possibly talk about her without mentioning the way we write? Egjaktli. Zii. I genuinely don't know how we ended up with our own little dictionary, but here we are. Replacing letters, spelling things the way they sound, and somehow making perfectly normal words look like they've been through something. It's such a silly little habit, but I love it. It's one of those things that probably wouldn't make much sense to anyone else, and that's exactly what makes it fun.

Then there's her creative side. I don't think I've ever properly told her how much I like the things she makes. The mandalas, the crafts, the drawings, all those little patterns and doodles. She has this way of making even the simplest designs look so pretty. Almost like something you'd save on Pinterest and then wonder how someone actually made it. I know she doesn't always get enough time for it, and I also know she once thought about posting her work but couldn't really manage doing it regularly. But I hope she knows that she doesn't need to turn something she enjoys into another responsibility. I just like that this side of her exists.

She loves nature too. The rain, the calm weather, beautiful places, all those little things that make the world feel a little quieter. She has this fondness for beautiful places across India, and I can understand why. If there's one thing I've gathered about her, it's that she doesn't need an awful lot to be happy. A little peace, a place she finds beautiful, and the people she genuinely wants around her. At least, that's how I see it. And if I'm being honest, I do wish I could be there to see some of those places with her.

Also, chocolate. I really don't think this needs much explanation. Especially chocolate-chip ice cream. Any kind of chocolate can probably make her day, and I find that quite funny in the nicest way possible. Then there's her favourite baby pink, her black and white palette, and her hair. Her natural curls look so perfect on her, but then she straightens it and looks just as good. I genuinely cannot pick one. It's a rather unfair situation, if you ask me.

She has her little quirks too. Her goldfish memory, for one. Although I know she laughs about it, I also know it bothers her sometimes, and she does want to improve it. So I'm not going to make a whole joke out of it. But it's one of those things that I associate with her. Then there's how her texts can suddenly become short when something is wrong, or how she sometimes goes completely blank when flirting catches her off guard and all she can manage is a 🙂 or 🙃. And if I mess something up, well, there's a good chance I'll get scolded like a mom. Which, honestly, I probably deserve sometimes.

But jokes aside, there's a lot more to her than these little habits. One thing I genuinely admire about her is how much she likes understanding things. She doesn't just want to hear an answer and move on. She wants to know why, how, and what actually happened. She likes looking at the whole picture, even when the truth might not be particularly pleasant. And I think that's something quite rare. She has her own opinions, and she cares about them being understood. She doesn't need someone to agree with everything she says, but she does deserve someone who actually listens and takes her thoughts seriously.

She's also someone who cares. And I don't mean that in some generic way where someone is called caring just because they're nice. I've seen how much importance she gives to understanding what's going on with someone, rather than simply assuming things. She listens. She tries to understand. And sometimes, even when a conversation is difficult, she doesn't just dismiss it because it's uncomfortable. She can take a step back and come back to it when things are easier. I've always appreciated that about her.

There's also something I find quite lovely about the way she is with the people she considers her own. Her relationship with her younger sister, for example. They're loving and supportive of each other, and somehow still manage to have their little arguments over who gets to be the elder one. I don't know how they even decide that, but it's such a sibling thing to do.

And I suppose that's what I mean when I say that she has so many little sides to her. There's the girl who can spend time making beautiful patterns, the one who gets excited over chocolate, the one who loves rain and beautiful places, the one who can talk for hours, and the one who can go completely silent when she doesn't know what to reply. There's the thoughtful side of her, the playful side, the slightly dramatic side, and the side that will probably scold me when I do something stupid. None of these things cancel each other out. They're all her.

I could keep adding things here, and I'm sure there are still so many little habits I've missed. But I think that's something I like about knowing her. There's always another little thing to notice. And sometimes it's not even something new. It's just something she has done a hundred times before, and somehow, the hundred-and-first time makes me appreciate it a little more.

I don't think she needs to be anything other than herself. She doesn't need to be less silly, more serious, more talkative, or anything else. There's no particular version of her that I'd rather have. It's all these little things, even the ones she might consider completely ordinary, that make her the person I've come to know.

And I really, really like that person.

✦
Chapter 5

Beyond What Meets the Eye

I think there's a lot about her that people might not really get to see. And honestly, even after knowing her for so long, I don't think I've discovered every little part of the way she thinks. There's so much more to her than just the fun-loving, playful side that I adore. The way she looks at things, the way she forms her opinions, the things she considers right and wrong, and the way she thinks about people and the world around her. These are things I find myself appreciating more and more whenever we get into one of our deeper conversations.

Something I've always found interesting about her is the way she approaches a difference of opinion. She usually goes quiet first. Not because she has nothing to say, but because she wants to understand what's being said before responding. She listens, thinks about it, and then speaks. And I really like that about her. She doesn't have to turn every disagreement into an argument, and she doesn't seem to be interested in proving herself right just for the sake of it. She takes her time, and I think there's something quite lovely about that.

Although, there's one thing I wish she wouldn't do as much. Sometimes she holds back her own opinions because she doesn't want me to feel like she's opposing me. And I really don't want that. I want to hear what she thinks, even if it's completely different from what I believe. She doesn't have to agree with me, and she certainly doesn't have to make her thoughts smaller just to avoid a disagreement. I want to know her perspective, even when it challenges mine. Because what's the point of having all these conversations if we're only going to say things the other person wants to hear? I love hearing her thoughts. All of them. And I hope she never forgets that.

There's also something about the way she looks at things that I've always admired. A lot of the things she's said have come from a rather selfless perspective. She tends to consider the moral side of things, the human side of things, and sometimes even what's better for everyone rather than just what's convenient for one person. And I don't think that's something I've appreciated enough. It's easy to look at situations through the lens of what we want, what benefits us, or what would make things easier for ourselves. But she often looks beyond that. She considers the people involved, the bigger picture, and what would actually be right. I find that genuinely beautiful about her.

And I think that's one of the things I love about our deeper conversations. It's not always about agreeing with each other or reaching some conclusion. Sometimes it's just about understanding how she sees something. The reasoning behind her opinions, the things she considers important, and the little details she notices that I might have completely overlooked. I like knowing how her mind works. I like hearing her explain something, even when I might have a different opinion initially. And sometimes, I find myself looking at something differently simply because she's made me consider another perspective.

I also love that she has her own opinions in the first place. She isn't someone whose thoughts should just be defined by the people around her. She has her own way of looking at things, her own understanding of what's right, and her own reasons for believing what she does. And even when she doesn't immediately express those thoughts, I know they're there. I want her to feel comfortable sharing them. Not just with me, but with anyone who genuinely wants to understand them. She deserves to have her opinions heard without feeling like she has to apologise for having them.

I suppose there's a lot I still want to learn about her. There are probably so many things she believes in that we haven't properly discussed, so many opinions I haven't heard, and so many perspectives of hers that I haven't had the chance to understand yet. And that's okay. I don't think knowing someone means having every answer about them. Sometimes it's just being interested enough to keep asking, keep listening, and keep discovering. We don’t have any rush, after all. It’s just us, for ever and ever.

And that's what I want with her. I don't just want to know the things she likes, the things that make her laugh, or the little habits that make her so unmistakably herself. I want to know how she sees the world. What makes her believe in something, what makes her question something, what she considers right, and what she wishes people understood a little better. I want to know the thoughts she doesn't always say out loud, and the reasons behind the opinions she holds.

Because there's so much more to her than what meets the eye. And I don't think I'll ever get tired of discovering it.

✦
Chapter 6

The Little Things You Do

I think there are quite a few things my love does that she probably doesn't even realise I've grown so fond of. And they're not necessarily big things either. Most of them are rather ordinary, actually. Little reactions, the way she responds to certain things, the way she shows that she cares... things that might not even cross her mind twice, but somehow stay with me. I don't know, I think when you get to know someone this closely, you start noticing things that you probably wouldn't have paid attention to otherwise. And with her, there's quite a lot of that.

For instance, I've started noticing how her texts change when something is wrong. Sometimes her replies just get shorter, and although she might not say anything directly, I can usually tell that something is a little off. I won't pretend I always know what's going on, because I don't. But it's something I've come to recognise. And I think it's rather funny how a person can become so familiar to you that even a small change in the way they text catches your attention.

Then there's the way she reacts when I catch her off guard. Especially when I'm being a little too sweet or flirting with her out of nowhere. Suddenly, my love has nothing to say. Absolutely nothing. And all I'm getting is a 🙂 or a 🙃. It's genuinely one of my favourite things. I don't even need a proper reply sometimes; that one little emoji tells me enough about how successfully I've managed to leave her speechless. Although, knowing her, she'll probably find a way to get back at me later.

And I really love how she pays attention to me. I don't think I've ever been particularly good at explaining what's going on in my head, especially when something is bothering me. But she does try to understand. I've shared parts of myself with her that I wasn't particularly comfortable talking about, and she never made me feel like I had to justify being the person I was at the time. She cared enough to understand me, and I don't think that's something I'll ever take lightly. We don't always have to reach some perfect conclusion or figure everything out in one conversation, either. We can leave something for later and come back to it when we're both in a better place to talk. I like that we can do that.

Of course, not everything about her is going to be all soft and sweet. If I mess something up, there's a good chance I'll get scolded. And honestly, sometimes I deserve it. She can be quite the mom when she wants to be, and I don't think I'll ever get used to that. Although I suppose that's partly my own fault. I do give her enough reasons.

And then there's the punishment she once decided was appropriate for me: commenting beautiful lines on her posts. I mean, really? That's what she came up with? Making me sit there and think of something pretty enough to leave under her pictures. And the funny part is that I actually did it. I don't think she could have picked a punishment that suited me any better, even if she tried. I'll admit, she got that one right.

I also love how happy a little effort can make her. Sometimes it's not even anything particularly special, just something small that I've put a little thought into. And seeing her appreciate it makes me want to do more of those things. Not because I think I have to keep coming up with something, but because I genuinely like making her happy. I like knowing that something I did, however small, made her day a little nicer.

And I suppose I should mention how she sometimes puts other people's feelings before her own, too. I've seen her do that with me. There have been times when she's had something of her own to share, but she'll first make sure I'm alright. She'll check on me and only then get around to telling me what she wanted to say. And I don't think she realises how much I notice that. I hope she also knows that she doesn't always have to put herself second. I want to hear her stories, her little updates, her good news, all of it. She deserves to have someone just as interested in what's happening with her.

I could probably keep going, honestly. There are things she says, things she does, and little reactions of hers that I haven't even thought of while writing this. And I'm sure I'll keep finding more of them. That's the thing, though. I don't think I need every little thing to be extraordinary for it to matter to me. Sometimes it's just her being her, and somehow that's enough to make an ordinary moment memorable.

Maybe she doesn't notice half of these things herself. Maybe some of them are so normal to her that she'd wonder why I'm even writing about them. But I wanted to. Because these are the things I get to know when I spend so much time with her, and they're the things I find myself remembering later.

I don't think she has to do anything differently. I just hope she never feels that the little things she does go unnoticed. Because they don't. Not by me.

✦
Part 3

What You Became to Me

Chapter 7

Somewhere Between Hello and Goodnight

The part after finding my home became a lot more exciting. The new shyness, along with the thrill of sharing our entire day with each other, slowly became a part of everyday life. Something we both got used to, but somehow, it never really felt ordinary. It felt like a choice we made every single day, something we genuinely looked forward to, rather than just another part of our routine.

The cheerfulness and the calm I felt whenever I heard that little “I lubbhh uu” made me look forward to hearing it. And strangely enough, I still do, even today. Which is funny, because I used to think it was just something people did. Like another little task at the end of the day, something you say before going to sleep.

But it never felt like that with her.

For such a long time, I'd wanted to know what it felt like to be somebody's priority. To be somebody's first choice, not just occasionally, but genuinely. And she made me experience that. For the first time in my life.

And it wasn't just in the words she said. It was in the little things she did, often without making a big deal out of them. I could send her five, six, sometimes seven messages or voice notes, and she'd go through every single one of them. She'd pay attention to what I was saying, notice how I was feeling, and respond to all of it. Even when she had something exciting of her own to share, she'd first make sure I was alright. And if I wasn't, she'd put her own news aside, listen to me, and sometimes save it for another time. Think about that for a moment. She could have had the best news to tell me, something she'd been waiting to share all day, and still, she'd make sure I was okay first.

I don't think she ever needed to announce that I mattered to her. I could see it in the way she made room for me in her day, in how she remembered the little things I'd said, and in how she made even an ordinary conversation feel like something we both wanted to be part of. It wasn't about having something interesting to talk about every day. Sometimes there wasn't much to say at all, and yet, there we were, finding our way from one hello to the next goodnight.

And I think that's what made it so special. I wasn't just someone she spoke to when she had nothing else to do. I felt included in her everyday life. I got to know about the little things that happened to her, the things that made her happy, the things that bothered her, and all those seemingly unimportant details that people don't necessarily think to share with everyone. And she got to know mine, too. There was something really lovely about knowing that, somewhere in her day, there was a little space that belonged to us.

I don't think I can properly explain what that felt like. It was something I'd wanted for so long, and then suddenly, there it was. Someone who wanted to hear from me, who made time for me, who cared about how my day had gone. Someone whose day I wanted to hear about just as much. And I loved that feeling. Maybe a little too much, even.

It almost felt like a drug. Something I found myself looking forward to every day, something I could never quite get enough of. And I know that sounds a little strange, but it felt so wrong to describe it that way, and yet so right at the same time. Because somewhere along the way, those little conversations stopped being just conversations. They became the part of my day I looked forward to the most. And even now, after all this time, the thought of hearing that little “I lubbhh uu” still brings back that same feeling.

I guess that's what I wanted all along. Not some grand gesture or a promise that I'd always come first. Just to feel that I had a place in someone's day, that my presence was wanted, and that someone was genuinely happy to have me there. And she gave me that feeling in ways she probably doesn't even realise.

✦
Chapter 8

My Favourite Kind of Quiet

Before meeting her, all I wanted was to be alone. Calm. Peaceful. With nobody around to disturb or interrupt that little bit of peace I had for myself. I always found people a little too... loud. Too much noise, too much happening, too many things demanding my attention. Life itself felt like something I had to get through, rather than something I could actually live and enjoy.

Little did I know, that was just the introduction. I hadn't even experienced what life could feel like with her in it.

Somewhere along the way, things started changing. She became a part of my everyday life, and then, slowly, a part of the way I looked at life itself. She made me realise that maybe peace didn't have to mean being away from everyone. Maybe I didn't always need to be by myself to feel at ease. And I think the biggest proof of that was how my definition of being alone changed.

Because eventually, being alone didn't just mean me, sitting somewhere quietly with my own thoughts. It meant me, along with her. Anywhere. Doing absolutely nothing, talking about absolutely nothing, or simply having her around. The place didn't matter much, and neither did what we were doing. If she was there, that was enough to make it feel like my kind of quiet.

And honestly, that's a little strange when I think about it. Because she isn't exactly the quietest person in the world, at least with me. She has this rather playful, sometimes chaotic side to her, and I wouldn't necessarily associate that with the kind of silence I used to look for. But that's where she surprised me. I realised that she could be both. She could be calm and peaceful when the moment called for it, and just as easily bring in all that playful cheerfulness when it was needed. And somehow, neither side takes away from the other.

I suppose I had misunderstood what I was looking for all along. I thought I wanted a life without noise, without interruptions, without anyone around. But what I really wanted was a place where I could feel at ease. And with her, I found that without having to ask her to be any different from who she is.

I don't need every moment with her to be exciting. I don't need us to have something planned, or a conversation going, or something to keep us occupied. I can just exist alongside her, and that's one of the nicest feelings I've come to know. It's funny how the person who brought so much more life into mine also became the person I associate with peace.

And if that's what being alone with someone can feel like, then I think I've found my favourite kind of quiet. It’s... her.

✦
Chapter 9

Things I Hope You Know

There's an endless list of things my heart wishes you knew, even without me having to say them out loud. Although, I do try. Because unlike those lucky people who can convey everything through their eyes, we have to make do with words.

I wish you could see yourself through my eyes, even if just for a moment. Maybe then you'd understand why I wrote all of this in the first place. This is just another little attempt at showing you my world, with you in it.

I hope you know how much you matter. Not just to me, but to everyone whose life you become a part of. How your presence, sometimes calm and sometimes full of cheer, makes an ordinary day a little better. I hope you know that you are enough, exactly as you are. That you don't have to change a single thing to deserve all the love and happiness coming your way.

And I hope you know that you're still the most beautiful girl in the whole wide world, even when you haven't taken a shower.

Especially then, perhaps.

I hope you know that I wouldn't want you any other way. You're already my perfect girl, just as you are.

✦
Chapter 10

The Year I Got to Know You

Okay, I'm writing this in the last few hours, and honestly, I feel bad. Because even though I made sure it wasn't rushed, finishing it in the eleventh hour does make it feel a little rushed. But it was all for one reason... to make you see you. The way you came across to me in this little span of a year. Even less, actually.

From talking about each other's loneliness to becoming the people who stand by each other. From teasing friends who'd casually go, "yeah, I judged you for it," to telling each other, "you can be free with me with your feelings... I'll never judge you." From late-night random memes to late-night love, still with the memes, of course. And honestly, I don't think I could've ever imagined any of this a year ago. It's been the best year, if I may say so. The worst as well, in certain ways, but with you by my side, the best always seems to come on top.

It's crazy how I found you, my soulmate, in the very same year I had sworn I'd never give anyone a chance. And yet, here you are. And I don't think I can give the credit for that to anything other than you, my love. The way you came into my life, the way we got to know each other, the way things just slowly became what they are today. I don't think I could've planned any of it, and I'm really, really glad I didn't have to.

You're the best person I've ever had the privilege of knowing. And the funny thing is, the more I get to know you, the more I realise there's still so much left to know. So many little things about you that I haven't quite figured out yet, so many things that make you who you are, and so many reasons I find myself loving you a little more. You have all these little complexities tucked beneath what might seem like a simple, beautiful exterior, and I don't think I could ever get tired of discovering them. Not even if I spent a lifetime doing so.

I suppose that's what I wanted this book to be. Not some grand description of how perfect you are, or a collection of reasons that somehow captures all of you. Because I don't think I could ever do that. Just a little something that lets you see how much of you I've gotten to know, how much of that I adore, and how genuinely happy I am that it was you I got to know in this lifetime.

Here's to the year I got to know you, my love. And I really, really hope I get to keep knowing you for a very, very long time. Possibly, forever.

I really hope you enjoyed all of this, and that I managed to make your birthday even a little more special. You deserve so much more than just one day of being celebrated, and I hope you never forget that.

And well, this is just one birthday. We have so many more ahead of us, and I fully intend to make each one just as special, if not more.

Happy birthday once again, my love. Here's to many, many more. ❤️
